ipcChannelsConfirmed.disposition: GAP RESOLVED for this file: exactly 10 ipcMain.handle registrations, all read. IMPORTANT boundary finding: core automation CRUD (create/update/delete/list/runNow on the primary — non-external — automation record) is NOT registered in this file. Source comment at :75-77 states 'Orca automation CRUD now arrives over the local runtime RPC surface, so the runtime methods take the lease through this hook instead of an arm here' — i.e. primary CRUD is dispatched over the same local-runtime-RPC transport E1's parent report and E3 already track under the web-factory/runtime-client surface, NOT classic Electron ipcMain/contextBridge. This leaf does not re-derive that RPC surface (excluded scope: 59 web factories/13 caller routes already closed elsewhere) but records the boundary fact here because it directly answers 'through explicit service boundary' for this card: the service boundary is bimodal — legacy external-manager/dispatch-result/precheck/scope-retention traffic over ipcMain, primary CRUD over the runtime RPC client.

errorGap.disposition: RESOLVED — a blocked dispatch DOES surface a visible reason on both the scheduled and manual paths, via two different, source-confirmed mechanisms:

scheduledPath.note: A scheduled occurrence that cannot start writes one run row per occurrence (folded by skip-coalescing only on byte-identical text, per the file's header comment) with status 'skipped_unavailable' and a fixed-sentence error (NO_RUNNABLE_HOST or the target-resolution error) — this row is what AutomationRunsTable/AutomationRunHistory render, i.e. genuinely visible to the user, not a silent no-op.

manualPath.note: Only the automation_target_removed conflict writes a run-history row (recordRefusedAutomationRun, called from runAutomationNowFenced's catch when error.code === targetRemoved); automation_owner_changed and automation_owner_fencing_required do NOT write a row by design (source comment: 'the CALLER is stale, and a client re-reading and retrying must not litter history'). All FOUR conflict codes (automation_owner_changed, automation_target_removed, automation_owner_fencing_required, automation_destination_invalid) are instead converted by the renderer's classify()/CONFLICT_RECOVERY map into a {status:'conflict', message, recovery} outcome, which automation-row-action-dispatch.ts turns into a rendered notice (severity:'owner') consumed by AutomationOwnerConflictNotice.tsx (has its own passing test file). recovery is one of 'retry'|'reconnect'|'update-server'|null and is executed by automation-host-recovery.ts (src/renderer/src/components/automations/automation-host-recovery.ts, sha256 6ba423e9f0c54e2cb8af0fbc37eec40916da9dee9bc97ec68382827e8c2867ef), which reuses SettingsNavigationTarget (this leaf's prior E1 leaf artifact, docs/migration/audit-closure/e1-ui/leaf/navigation.json) to route 'update-server' to the Servers/SSH settings pane.

recoveryGap.disposition: RESOLVED — a crashed/interrupted run is NOT left stuck 'running' forever.
recoveryGap.note: At authority startup, non-terminal retained runs are staged into a pending map; a periodic sweep (2s interval, unref'd so it never keeps the process alive) re-attempts attach() until the terminal surface reports ready, then applies a 2-minute settle grace (SURFACE_SETTLE_MS) before calling strand() on anything still unresolved. strand() (wired in run-completion-watcher.ts:62-68) finalizes the run with status:'dispatch_failed' and a describeStrandedAutomationRun() message. This mirrors the AGENTS.md-mandated live/unverifiable/exited discipline: a pane that has not been proven gone is 'not known yet' (kept pending), never treated as evidence of loss, until the grace window elapses.
